title: 7 ICT concepts every trader actually needs
caption: ICT has 100 concepts. You need 7. The ones that survive contact with a live account. Save this.

slides.definition: The last opposing candle before a strong move. Institutions filled orders here; price returns to it because liquidity remains. Mark it on D1/H4 only.
slides.example: Up-move started here? The last red candle is your demand zone.

slides.definition: A 3-candle imbalance where price moved too fast to trade fairly. Price tends to return and fill it. A magnet, not a guarantee.
slides.example: Gap between candle 1's high and candle 3's low = the FVG.

slides.title: Liquidity sweep
slides.body: Price spikes past an obvious high/low (where stops sit), grabs the liquidity, then reverses. The trap is the signal. Stop-hunts are not random — they're the setup.

slides.title: Market structure shift
slides.body: A break of the most recent swing in the opposite direction. This is your only real confirmation that the prior trend just died. No MSS, no entry.

slides.title: Premium / discount
slides.body: Draw a fib on the range. Only sell in premium (top half), only buy in discount (bottom half). Most retail losses come from buying in premium.

slides.title: Killzones
slides.body: London open and NY open carry the moves. Setups outside these windows have worse follow-through. Time is a filter, not an afterthought.

slides.title: One A+ a day
slides.body: The 7th concept is discipline. D1 bias → H4 zone → H1 confirmation → one trade. The edge isn't the concepts. It's not taking the other 12 setups.

slides.sub: The setups + the rules. Free PDF.
